title: Al-Hadi, the Guide
tomorrow: a blank wall, no sketch to copy. where does anything begin?

cards: Miss a turn and a map app doesn't scold you. A calm voice says rerouting, and finds a new way from exactly where you are. Yesterday's question: Eli has a blank page and a deadline, so who shows him the way?
Amira does, a little. She sits with him at a table in the shop and they spread his drawings out. But she won't always be around.
Today's Name is the Guide who doesn't leave.

teach.b: Al-Hadi, the Guide. The Fatiha, which Muslims recite in their daily prayers, asks for exactly this, in Pickthall's words: "Show us the straight path." Here's the thing to tell a friend tonight: the request is plural.
Even someone praying alone at midnight asks for the path on behalf of more than one person.
Now the week's Names, walking that path together. Al-Ghaniyy: he needs nothing, so the thank you was for our own soul.
Al-Mughni: he enriches, with more and with enough, the way Amira learned to be glad about Eli's sketchbook. Al-Mani': harm withheld, the rained-out paint day.
Ad-Darr: all is in his hand, Dadi's ache and Dadi's patience. An-Nafi': benefit, the water that stays when the foam is gone. An-Nur: light, enough for the next step.
And today the Guide, who gives that light a direction. Guidance in this picture isn't a full map handed over at the start. It's one turn at a time, and a calm rerouting when a turn gets missed.

how: In their daily prayers, Muslims recite al-Fatiha, asking ihdina as-sirat al-mustaqim: guide us on the straight path.

o: the Watcher, who notes each turn
the Guide, who shows the path
the Judge, who weighs each step

games.q: the week's Names on one path — tap the pairs.

s: the Fatiha asks 'show me the path,' in the singular
"Show us the straight path." the request is plural, even when prayed alone.
in the parable of the rain, what is of use to mankind remains in the earth
the foam passes away; the useful water stays.
Al-Ghaniyy means God needs our prayers to stay strong
He needs nothing; Solomon said thanks is for the good of one's own soul.

games.q: a younger cousin keeps asking you to decide everything for her: classes, friends, even what to post. what fits this week's Names?
o: help with the next step, and point her toward asking for guidance herself.
decide it all for her; being that useful is what benefit means.
refuse to help at all; she has to find the way on her own.
games.why: guidance here comes one turn at a time, and the prayer for it is plural. helping someone take a step isn't the same as walking it for them.

practice: If there's room, stand and walk slowly for a minute, across the room or down a hallway. With each step, say inwardly, guide me, or simply notice where each foot lands.
Then sit for the rest of the time, facing the way you were walking.

wordCard.voice: Al-Hadi. The Guide, who shows the path and gives the next step, and reroutes when a turn is missed.

orig.note: Arabic: the Guide, a Name of Allah; the Fatiha's ihdina, guide us, comes from the same root.

carryVoice: Keep it close: guide me, and, the way the Fatiha says it, guide us. That's two weeks of Names.

sources.ref: Qur'an 25:31 (Allah suffices as Guide and Helper)
